\label{lemma:pair-of-maps}
  Suppose that $\nu$ is a $\sigma$-finite $\alpha$-homogeneous measure
  on $(\mathbb{X},\mathfrak{B})$ and that Assumption~\ref{assumption:X} is
  satisfied.  For $x \in \mathbb{X}$, define $\tau(x) \in \mathbb{R}_{++}$ by the
  requirement that $\tau(x)^{-1}x\in\mathbb{S}$.  Then the following hold.
  \begin{itemize}
  \item[i)] The maps $(x,t)\mapsto tx$ from $\mathbb{S}\times\mathbb{R}_{++}$ to
    $\mathbb{X}$ and $x\mapsto(\tau(x)^{-1}x,\tau(x))$ from $\mathbb{X}$ to
    $\mathbb{S}\times\mathbb{R}_{++}$ are mutually inverse.
  \item[ii)] If $\mathfrak{B}$ is $\nu$-complete, then
    $x\mapsto(\tau(x)^{-1}x,\tau(x))$ is $\mathfrak{B} / \mathfrak{B}_{| \mathbb{S}}
    \otimes \mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R}_{++})$-measurable, where $\mathfrak{B}_{| \mathbb{S}}$ is the
    $\sigma$-algebra induced by $\mathfrak{B}$ on $\mathbb{S}$.
  \item[iii)] If $(\mathbb{X},\mathfrak{B})$ is a Borel space, then
    $x\mapsto(\tau(x)^{-1}x,\tau(x))$ is $\mathfrak{B} / \mathfrak{B}_{| \mathbb{S}}
    \otimes \mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R}_{++})$-measurable.
  \end{itemize}

\textsl{Necessity.} Enumerate $\mathcal{H}$ as $\{h_n\}_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$. Assume
  that for all $x \in \mathbb{X}$ the function $t \mapsto h_n(tx)$ is 
	right-continuous in $t\in\mathbb{R}_{++}$.  Denote by $\mathbb{Q}_{++}$ the set of
  strictly positive rational numbers. For $n,k,j\in\mathbb{N}$ and
  $r\in\mathbb{Q}_{++}$, define
  \begin{displaymath}
    U_{nkrj}:=\{x\in\mathbb{S}:\; h_n(sx)\geq 2^{-k},\; s\in[r,r+2^{-j}]\}.
  \end{displaymath}
  Since $B:=\{x \in \mathbb{S}:\;h_n(x)\geq 2^{-k}\} \in \mathfrak{B}$, the
	right-continuity property and Remark~\ref{remark:scaling-one-s} yield that
  \begin{displaymath}
    U_{nkrj}=\bigcap_{s\in\mathbb{Q}\cap[r,r+2^{-j}]}s^{-1}B\in \mathfrak{B}.
  \end{displaymath}

  Put $J_{rj} :=[r,r+2^{-j}]$. Then $J_{nj} U_{nkrj} \in \mathfrak{B}^\nu$
  and, by \eqref{eq:nu-h-integral},
  \begin{displaymath}
    \nu(J_{nj} U_{nkrj}) 
    \leq 2^k \int_{J_{nj} U_{nkrj}} h_n(x) \, \nu(dx)
    \leq 2^k \int_\mathbb{X} h_n(x) \, \nu(dx)<\infty.
  \end{displaymath}
  
  Put $\mathbb{S}' = \bigcup_{n,k,r,j} U_{nkrj}$.  If $x\in\mathbb{S}\setminus\mathbb{S}'$,
  $n,k,j \in \mathbb{N}$, and $r \in \mathbb{Q}_{++}$, there exists $s \in
  [r,r+2^{-j}]$ (depending on $x,n,k,r,j$) such that $h_n(s
  x)<2^{-k}$.  The right-continuity of $t \mapsto h_n(t x)$ yields
  that $h_n(r x)=0$ for all $r\in\mathbb{Q}_{++}$ and thence $h_n(tx)=0$ for
  all $t\in\mathbb{R}_{++}$.
	
  Enumerate $(U_{nkrj}, J_{rj})$, $n,k,j\in\mathbb{N}$ and $r\in\mathbb{Q}_{++}$, as
  $(W_n, I_n)$, $n \in \mathbb{N}$, so that $\mathbb{S}' = \bigcup_{n \in \mathbb{N}} W_n$
  and $\nu(I_n W_n)< \infty$ for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$.  By
  \eqref{Eq:nu-support-h}, the measure $\nu$ assigns all of its mass
  to the set $\mathbb{X}':= (0,\infty) \mathbb{S}' \in \mathfrak{B}^\nu$, and the result
  follows from the decomposition of $\nu$ guaranteed by
  Proposition~\ref{proposition:renorm} and
  Proposition~\ref{proposition:sphere}.  Finally,
  \eqref{Eq:levy-condition-pi-general} follows from the change of
  variables in \eqref{eq:nu-h-integral} using the polar decomposition of
  $\nu$ as $\pi\otimes\theta_\alpha$.

  If all functions $h_n(tx)$ are left continuous in $t\in\mathbb{R}_{++}$,
  then the definition of $U_{nkrj}$ should be modified by working with
  the interval $[r-2^{-j},r]$ for $2^{-j}<r$. 

  \textsl{Sufficiency} is immediate by checking that the measure $\nu$
  defined by \eqref{Eq:nu-rep} is $\alpha$-homogeneous.

  a Poisson process $\{\eta_i : i \in \mathbb{N}\}$, where the sum is
  appropriately defined by using principal values and compensating
  terms if necessary, see \cite[Th.~7.2]{dav:mol:zuy08}.
  Theorem~\ref{thr:levy-k-separating-countable} establishes that
  $\{\eta_i : i \in \mathbb{N}\}$ can be constructed as
  $\{\Gamma_i^{-1/\alpha}\varepsilon_i: i \in \mathbb{N}\}$, that is, as randomly
  scaled i.i.d. copies of a random element $\varepsilon$.

\label{ex:processes-values}
  Let $\mathbb{K}$ be the family $\mathbb{R}^{[0,\infty)}$ of real valued-functions
  on $\mathbb{R}_+$ with the cylindrical $\sigma$-algebra, the pointwise arithmetic
  addition of functions as the semigroup operation, involution being
  the negation, and the scaling operation applied pointwise.
	It is known \cite{kab:stoev12,mar70} that an infinitely
  divisible separable in probability stochastic process $\xi(s)$,
  $s\in\mathbb{R}_+$, can be associated with the Poisson process
  $\{\eta_i,i\in\mathbb{N}\}$ on $\mathbb{R}^{[0,\infty)}$ with a $\sigma$-finite
  intensity measure $\nu$, so that $\xi$ admits a L\'evy measure
  $\nu$. If $\xi$ is symmetric, then, for each $s\in\mathbb{R}_+$,
  \begin{equation}
    \label{eq:id-processes}
    \xi(s)\overset{d}{\sim} \lim_{r\downarrow 0}\sum_{|\eta_i(t)|\geq r}
    \eta_i(s),\qquad s\in\mathbb{R}_+,
  \end{equation}
  where $\overset{d}{\sim}$ in this setting denotes the equality of all
  finite-dimensional distributions.  It should be noted that the order
  of summands in \eqref{eq:id-processes} may change with $t$, and
  there might be no order of the summands that guarantees the
  convergence for all rational $s$, not to say for all
  $s\in\mathbb{R}_+$. Such a common order exists for random functions with
  non-negative values (in which case $\mathbb{K}$ is endowed with the
  identical involution).
  
  This cone does not admit a countable separating family of
  characters.  Let $\tilde{\mathbb{K}}$ be the countable family of characters
  defined by
  \begin{equation}
    \label{Eq:chi-line}
    \chi(x)=e^{\imath x(s) u},\qquad s\in\mathbb{Q}_+,
  \end{equation}
  where $x=(x(s))_{s\geq 0}$ is an element of $\mathbb{R}^{[0,\infty)}$ and
  $u$ belongs to the set $\mathbb{Q}$ of rational numbers.  
  Theorem~\ref{thr:levy-k-separating-countable} applies to the process
  $\xi$ restricted onto the set $\mathbb{Q}_+$ of non-negative rationals, so
  that the image $\tilde{\nu}$ of the L\'evy measure $\nu$ under the
  map that restricts a function to $\mathbb{Q}_+$ has polar decomposition as
  $\pi\otimes\theta_\alpha$ and the Poisson process with intensity
  $\tilde{\nu}$ is given by
  $\{\Gamma_i^{-1/\alpha}\tilde{\varepsilon}_i,i\geq1\}$. By
  \cite[Prop.~2.19]{kab:stoev12}, for each $t\in\mathbb{R}_+\setminus\mathbb{Q}_+$,
  the separability property of $\xi$ yields that
  $\Gamma_i^{-1/\alpha}\tilde{\varepsilon}_i(t_n)$ converges in probability
  to $\eta_i(t)$, whence $\tilde{\varepsilon}_i(t_n)$ converges in
  probability to $\varepsilon_i(t):=\Gamma_i^{1/\alpha}\eta_i(t)$. Thus, the
  L\'evy measure $\nu$ corresponds to the Poisson process
  $\{\Gamma_i^{-1/\alpha}\varepsilon_i,i\geq1\}$, where $\{\varepsilon_i,i\in\mathbb{N}\}$
  is a sequence of i.i.d. separable processes distributed as
  $\varepsilon(s)$, $s\in\mathbb{R}_+$. Condition \eqref{eq:eps-condition} in this
  setting is equivalent to $\mathbb{E}|\varepsilon(s)|^\alpha<\infty$ for all
  $s$. 

  In the symmetric case, following \eqref{eq:xi-r}, the convergence in
  \eqref{eq:id-processes} can be rephrased as
  \begin{displaymath}
    \xi(s)\overset{d}{\sim} \lim_{r\uparrow\infty} \sum_{\Gamma_i\leq r} 
    \Gamma_i^{-1/\alpha}\varepsilon_i(s),\qquad s\in\mathbb{R}_+.
  \end{displaymath}
  Therefore, in case of symmetric $\alpha$-stable processes the order
  of summands in \eqref{eq:id-processes} can be made the same for all
  time points. This makes it possible to appeal to path
  regularity results for stochastic integrals from
  \cite[Th.~4]{ros89p} in order to confirm that $\varepsilon$ shares path
  regularity properties with $\xi$, for instance, $\varepsilon$ is almost
  surely right-continuous with left limits (c\`adl\`ag) if $\xi$ is
  c\`adl\`ag. The same holds for stochastic processes with almost
  surely non-negative values, since then the involution is the
  identity. The pointwise convergence of the LePage series yields the
  uniform convergence, see \cite{bas:ros13}. Note that a result
  concerning the existence of the series representation of a general
  (not necessarily symmetric stable) infinitely divisible c\`adl\`ag
  function using c\`adl\`ag summands is not available.
